title: Sandpile avalanches in two dimensions are finite
summary: In the abelian sandpile model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, a site with at least $2d$ grains topples by sending one grain to each neighbor. In a box $[-N,N]^d$ whose boundary absorbs grains, adding grains at random sites and toppling defines a Markov chain. Athreya and Járai (2004) constructed the stationary state on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ as the limit of its stationary distributions as $N\to\infty$. They asked whether, when a grain is added at the origin of a sandpile in the stationary state, the resulting avalanche of topplings is finite. Járai and Redig (2008) proved that the answer is yes for $d\geq 3$,…
